A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Activation-Guided Consensus Merging (ACM). Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and response-length experiments on Qwen and LLaMA models, alongside ablations, reflection statistics, and a reasoning case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds calibration robustness results, an IFEval evaluation, and results using LIMO calibration data.

M1.justification: The layer activations, pretrained/fine-tuned mutual information, sigmoid weighting, and task-vector aggregation remain unchanged in Section 3. Discussion of alternative similarity measures and additional calibration experiments does not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds instruction-following evaluation on IFEval and LIMO as an alternative mathematical calibration corpus (Section 5 and Appendix A.4). Existing mathematical reasoning, code generation, and commonsense benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including the arithmetic, activation-based, DPO, and RL-based comparisons. IFEval extends the existing TIES comparison to another task. KL divergence and cosine similarity are discussed without adding evaluated merging baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds calibration-size controls of 20–300 examples, random/10/20/30 clustering conditions, and 1.5B IFEval evaluation with prompt-level and instruction-level scores. Existing evaluation defaults remain unchanged. Calibration-study attribution is unclear: Section 5 names the 1.5B series, but Table 4's 100-example result, 92.2 accuracy and 538.3 length, duplicates the 7B GSM8K entry in Table 1.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.4 substantially expand analysis of ACM's dependence on calibration design, testing sample count, cluster count, sampling seeds, and replacement of s1K with LIMO (Tables 4–6 and 12). These investigate previously untested robustness questions about a central component. Earlier hyperparameter analysis, reflection statistics, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that main scores average five runs with different random seeds. v2 additionally reports individual accuracy and length results for three calibration-sampling seeds on the 7B model in Table 5. This adds variability reporting without establishing an increase in the original run count; confidence intervals and significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: Existing matched results are unchanged. Added results include calibration sensitivity and seed outcomes, plus IFEval scores of 18.48/30.58 for TIES versus 20.15/31.06 for ACM-TIES (Table 7). Table 12 adds LIMO-calibrated ACM-TA results of 76.9 on GSM8K and 22.3 on Minerva Math; its other rows reproduce earlier results. These supplement the evidence under new conditions rather than revise same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a numerical demonstration of KL asymmetry: P = [0.9, 0.1] and Q = [0.5, 0.5] yield directional divergences of approximately 0.368 and 0.511. This is a limited addition to mathematical justification; the activation-weight salience derivation, MI definition, and merging equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free, layer-specific merging, improved reasoning efficiency, and plug-and-play applicability. The headline 55.3% length reduction and 1.3-point accuracy improvement are unchanged; new experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds reasons for choosing MI over KL divergence and cosine similarity. It interprets calibration stabilization near 100 examples and improved clustering results as evidence of robustness and reduced data imbalance, and describes adaptability to LIMO. Existing large-model tradeoffs and limitations concerning dense, same-architecture models remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces promised future code availability with a repository link. Section 5 adds a rough merging runtime of tens of seconds to one or two minutes depending on model size. Conversely, v2 removes v1's NVIDIA L40S GPU disclosure. Existing precision, sequence-length, sampling, and default hyperparameter details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Visual Agents as Fast and Slow Thinkers, LIMO, and IFEval. These provide limited additional context and support the added datasets; the positioning relative to existing model-merging approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: expanded metric-choice explanation, additional analysis headings, a new calibration appendix subsection, acknowledgments, and updated affiliations and conference text. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact tables in Section 5 and the calibration-corpus table in Appendix A.4. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and locally repositioned, while all six figures and the retained table designs remain unchanged. The visual changes are additions and reflow rather than a broad redesign.

improvement.justification: The added calibration tests address previously unexamined sensitivity of ACM's central calibration procedure, while IFEval broadens validation and the repository link improves access information. These provide a limited overall gain. Ambiguous model attribution in the new calibration tables and removal of the GPU specification weaken reproducibility, preventing a stronger assessment; the original method and principal results remain unchanged.
